text:
maya: Anyone else seeing weird host->device memcpy gaps on an Nsight timeline for batcher-v2? I captured a 30s nsight run and there are repeated pauses where the device is idle while memcpy waits happen later.

sam: Can you paste the waterfall excerpt? Screenshot helps but a text snippet is fine.

maya: Pasting a quick timeline excerpt from the capture (trimmed):
```
Device 0 stream 1: memcpy H2D [0.00ms - 2.34ms]
Device 0 stream 0: kernel conv_fwd [2.34ms - 8.90ms]
Device 0 stream 1: memcpy H2D [15.12ms - 17.53ms]
CPU thread (batcher submit): sleep [8.90ms - 15.12ms]  <-- gap where device is idle
Device 0 stream 0: kernel conv_fwd [17.53ms - 23.80ms]
```

li: that gap looks like the host submit thread got preempted between the first kernel finish and the next memcpy. Are the submit threads pinned? Also did you use cudaMemcpyAsync or sync memcpy?

maya: We use cudaMemcpyAsync into stream 1 and then kernel dispatch on stream 0. Submit threads are pinned to core 7 in the container however nsight shows hostspin wakeups coinciding with the memcpy starts.

jordan: Any difference when using a dedicated copy stream versus interleaving copy+compute on the same stream? Also worth testing stream priorities.

nina: I ran a short repro toggling KV cache prefetch: prefetch=on produced these numbers, prefetch=off was better. Quick perf summary: 
```
prefetch=on: p99 end-to-end 12.3ms, noticeable host gap ~5-7ms
prefetch=off: p99 end-to-end 8.1ms, device almost continuous
```
Seems prefetching introduced more host-side submit bursts.

perf-bot: Uploaded /tmp/nsight/1719990000_report.sqlite to s3://perf-traces/batcher-v2/1719990000_report.sqlite

sam: Could be either host scheduling or the pinned pool fallback. Do we see pagefaults or host allocations in the trace? Try cudaHostRegister on the buffers to rule out implicit pinning. Also run perfetto with sched events to correlate CPU preemption.

maya: Good call. I'll rerun with explicit cudaHostRegister and NVTX scopes around submit. Checklist I'm using:
1) NVTX around the submit region
2) cudaHostRegister on input buffers (avoid implicit pinning)
3) set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and isolate submit thread affinity
4) run nsight with CPU sampling at 1kHz and perfetto to capture sched_wakeup/sched_switch

li: If CPU preemption still shows up we should try a short experiment: move the submit into a SCHED_FIFO thread as a probe to see if gaps vanish. If they do, it's definitely host scheduling.

jordan: Also compare kernel selection impact — we saw earlier that int8 kernels launch more short-fused kernels which can increase host-launch rate, exposing scheduling sensitivity. Try forcing the fp16 kernel variant for a run.

nina: One more datapoint: when I disabled the KV prefetch path the memcpy pattern changed — copies were smaller and more frequent, but overall device utilization improved. So kernel selection + prefetching heuristics interact here.

maya: OK I'll run a matrix: prefetch on/off x kernel variant (int8/fp16) x hostregister on/off and post traces. Will upload timelines and perfetto slices.

sam: When you post, include the exact git sha and runtime config (cuda driver version, docker image, batch sizes). Small env differences matter.

maya: noted, will include reproducible command and env. Thanks. :thinking:

li: I'll take the first follow-up run this afternoon and post the traceid.

jordan: If we confirm scheduling is root cause, we can either reduce host launch rate (coalesce submits), move prefetch off the critical path, or move submit to a higher-priority thread as mitigation.

nina: +1 on coalescing and investigate batching heuristic to avoid many tiny prefetches.

maya: Thanks everyone — if the repro holds I'll open a short action item list and link traces in a follow-up thread.
